children: The U.K-based neocloud provider Nscale filed its initial public offering prospectus with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday.
The company applied to appear on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker NSCL. The filing did not include an expected price range or the number of stocks to be offered. Goldman Sachs
will act as lead bookrunners for the proposed offering.
Nscale has data centers in the U.K., Norway and Texas, with several more partner-run data centers operating in Europe and the U.S.

"We serve some of the largest companies on Earth through strategic partnerships and long-term agreements," Nscale founder and CEO Josh Payne noted in the filing. "This is the foundation that funds the continued buildout of our global footprint, and we believe the opportunity ahead here is vast. With a 10 GW+ portfolio of owned and controlled power, we expect significant expansion in Nscale Infrastructure as we grow with our existing customers, and contract and scale new customers building and delivering frontier intelligence."

As of August 31, 2026, the company's infrastructure portfolio included about 25,000 active GPUs and 461,000 active and contracted GPUs, along with five active and 12 contracted data center sites. What's more, the company had $2.6B of active and $103.4B of active and contracted TCV under long-term take-or-pay contracts with customers, compared to $500M of active and $38B of active and contracted TCV at the end of 2025. Nscale relies almost exclusively on Nvidia
GPUs. The company has signifcant contracts with Microsoft

Revenue for the first six months of 2026 totaled $140.6M, compared to $10.4M during the same period in 2025. The company also incurred a net loss of $1.02B for the first six months of 2026 due to substantial investments the company has made to grow its platform.

title: Nvidia-backed neocloud Nscale files for IPO
